inflation_management: Antarctica has no economy, currency or central bank: the 1959 Antarctic Treaty System reserves the continent for peaceful scientific use, and the 1991 Madrid Protocol bans mineral resource activity. There is no GDP, no debt and no inflation to manage - national programs fund research stations from home-country budgets, and the only commercial activity of scale is regulated tourism. Macroeconomic commentary does not apply.
debt_management: No sovereign, no borrowing, no debt statistics exist for Antarctica. Station-operating nations carry the costs on their own balance sheets. The relevant 'balance sheet' question is geopolitical: who funds presence on the continent, which under the Treaty cannot support sovereignty claims made after 1959.

key_events.event: October: the Ross Sea marine protected area was established under CCAMLR, the world's largest MPA.
December: COVID-19 reached Antarctica at Chile's Bernardo O'Higgins base, ending the continent's virus-free status.
Steady growth in regulated tourism and in Chinese and other new research stations, raising Treaty-system governance questions.

outlook_next_decade: The Madrid Protocol's mining ban is reviewable after 2048, but no near-term change is expected; the Treaty system held through the period. The pressures to watch are tourism growth, bioprospecting disputes, and great-power station-building as strategic positioning. Scientifically the continent's importance (climate, sea-level data) will only rise; economically it will remain a cost centre for claimant and research nations.
caveat: Outlook is an analytical assessment as of October 2026, not a forecast. 2025 figures are IMF estimates/projections.
